newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 18.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.
- EU leaders reached broad agreement on a new treaty but diplomats said it fell far short of both expectations and the requirements of enlarging the Union.
- The possibility of Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern meeting a Sinn Fein delegation before he becomes Prime Minister next week has almost completely receded.
- An oil painting by Paul Henry set a new record for the artist at a London auction.
- A 5.2 million sterling rights issue at a fraction of the last traded price is to be part of a massive restructuring of Mackie International.
- The EU ended its Amsterdam summit with an agreement that paves the way for up to 12 new countries to join.
- A wave of outrage swept the country over Sinn Fein's refusal to condemn the murder of two RUC men.
- The incoming government is facing a new crime crisis after another vicious murder in Dublin's O'Connell street.
- The Rape Crisis centre last night expressed alarm that a man serving a seven-year sentence for rape was released after just 12 months.
- Catholics in Northern Irleand are bracing themlseves for potentially bloody retribution after the IRA's slaughter of two RUC police.
- Ireland's battle to keep its place at the European Commission table in a new EU trreaty appeared to have been won late last night.
- A nationwide alert continued last night for an escaped British murderer believed to be hiding in Ireland.
